gap_map.why_it_matters: Router scaffolding produces endpoints fast. Nothing decides which of them carry business rules worth testing, so the suite ends up asserting that FastAPI can serialize a model.
gap_map.filled_by: LambdaTest/agent-skills#pytest-skill for authoring, trailofbits/skills#property-based-testing for invariants

gap_map.why_it_matters: The listed skills stop at the request/response boundary. Schema changes are the single most common source of irreversible production damage in this stack.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor requires every schema change to ship with a reversible migration and a plan for the deploy window.

layers.name: unit
layers.belongs_here: business rules and pure functions, called directly
layers.does_not_belong_here: anything needing a request or a database
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: the test spins up TestClient to check one calculation

layers.name: integration (TestClient)
layers.belongs_here: the real request path: dependency overrides, validation, serialisation and status codes
layers.does_not_belong_here: exhaustive branch coverage of business rules
layers.cost: moderate; this is where most real bugs are caught in this stack

layers.name: contract
layers.belongs_here: that the OpenAPI schema still matches what consumers rely on
layers.cost: cheap once wired, and it catches breaking changes nothing else sees

layers.name: e2e
layers.belongs_here: flows against a real database and real dependencies

testing.proportions: No proportions stated by the FastAPI team. The stack's own shape argues for weight at the TestClient layer: dependency overrides, validation and serialisation are where FastAPI applications actually break.
rules: Prefer TestClient over mocking the router. It exercises dependency resolution, validation and serialisation - the three things that break in production.
Override dependencies with app.dependency_overrides rather than patching module globals, and clear it between tests.
Test the boundary of every validation rule, not just the happy value.
Async endpoints need an async-aware runner. Read pyproject.toml before assuming pytest is configured for it.
traps: app.dependency_overrides left uncleared leaks into the next test, so a later test passes for the wrong reason.
A sync def endpoint doing blocking I/O runs in a threadpool and passes every test, then serialises under load.
Reusing the ORM model as a response model: the test passes and the endpoint quietly returns password hashes or internal flags.
A test database created per test but sharing a session with the app means the app sees uncommitted state - or does not see committed state.
Pydantic v1 and v2 behave differently on validation and serialisation; a test written against one is not evidence about the other.
what_not_to_test: That FastAPI validates a declared type or that it returns 422 for a bad body - that tests the framework.
Generated OpenAPI structure, beyond the contract points consumers depend on.
Alembic migration modules themselves; test the resulting schema instead.
testing.notes: Prefer FastAPI's TestClient for integration tests over mocking the router - it exercises dependency overrides, validation and serialization, which is where the real bugs are. Read pyproject.toml for the configured runner and typechecker before assuming these commands.

growth_thresholds.extract_service_layer: an endpoint function exceeds 40 lines, which means business logic has leaked into the transport layer
growth_thresholds.extract_package: >=2 features import the same internal module

layers.name: app/main.py
layers.holds: the FastAPI instance and include_router calls, plus app-wide dependencies
layers.must_not: path operations of its own beyond a root endpoint

layers.name: app/routers/
layers.holds: one module per resource, each exposing an APIRouter with its prefix, tags, dependencies and responses set at router level
layers.must_not: business rules - an endpoint function past ~40 lines has absorbed the service layer

layers.name: app/dependencies.py
layers.holds: shared dependencies used by more than one router
layers.must_not: feature-specific dependencies, which belong with their router

layers.name: app/internal/
layers.holds: routers not part of the public API surface

layers.name: service layer
layers.holds: business rules, callable without a request object

variants.name: The documented layout (app/ with routers/ and dependencies.py)
variants.use_when: the default; it is what the FastAPI docs describe for bigger applications
variants.cost: routers/ is a type-based folder, so a feature's router, schemas and service end up in three places

variants.name: Package per feature, each with its own router
variants.use_when: features are independent and each owns its schemas, service and data access
variants.cost: you leave the documented layout, so newcomers who read the FastAPI tutorial will not recognise it

variants.name: Explicit service layer between routers and data
variants.use_when: business rules are reused by more than one endpoint, or by a background job
variants.cost: one more hop for trivial CRUD; premature for an app that is mostly pass-through

rules: Set prefix, tags, dependencies and responses on the APIRouter, not repeated on every path operation.

Use relative imports within the package, and import the submodule rather than the name: `from .routers import items, users`. Importing `router` from each module overwrites the previous one - the docs call this out explicitly.
An endpoint function handles transport. Once it holds branching business logic it belongs in a function that can be called without a Request.
Pydantic models are the request/response contract. Do not reuse the database model as the response model - it leaks columns you did not mean to expose.
Every schema change ships with a reversible migration and a stated deploy order.
architecture.component_library: Not applicable. Shared dependencies go in app/dependencies.py once a second router needs them - not before.
architecture.notes: The FastAPI docs describe routers/ and dependencies.py, which is a type-first layout for a small app. For larger applications the mentor may propose package-per-feature, but must say that this departs from the documented structure.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: FastAPI supports both, and the wrong choice is invisible until the service is under load.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: async def with async-capable drivers throughout; sync def only when the library has no async version.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: A sync endpoint doing blocking I/O passes every test and serialises requests in production.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: FastAPI bundles no persistence and no migration tool.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: SQLAlchemy with Alembic unless the team has a reason otherwise.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Schema changes without a reversible migration are the most common cause of irreversible production damage in this stack.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: FastAPI's documented layout has routers and dependencies, and no service layer, so nothing stops logic accumulating in endpoints.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Logic in endpoints while they stay thin; extract a service the moment a rule is needed by a second caller.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Business rules trapped in endpoint functions can only be tested through HTTP, which makes every rule expensive to verify.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Security utilities are provided; the policy is not.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Decide the mechanism once and attach the authorization decision to every router, including 'public on purpose'.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Per-endpoint authorization added ad hoc leaves gaps nothing surfaces.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Deployment shape determines worker model, startup cost and how configuration is delivered.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Decide before building: serverless in particular constrains startup time and background work.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Background tasks and in-process caches that work under a long-lived worker silently do nothing under serverless.

operability.observability: Structured logging plus an exception handler registered on the app. Without a handler an unhandled error becomes a 500 with nothing recorded.
operability.authorization: A dependency on the path operation, or middleware. An endpoint with no security dependency is public - and looks identical to one that is public on purpose.
done_checks: the app boots with the real configuration
clean install from a fresh clone
rules: Every path operation states its authorization decision explicitly.
Every outbound call has a timeout. httpx without one waits forever and takes a worker with it.
Database sessions are per request and always closed, including on the error path.
Configuration is validated at boot, not read ad hoc with os.environ.get scattered through modules.
Schema changes ship with a reversible migration and a plan for the deploy window.

dead_code_risks: Endpoints registered by decorator and reachable only over HTTP
Pydantic models referenced only as type annotations in signatures
Alembic migration modules discovered by directory scan
Dependencies wired through Depends() with a callable reference
Celery or background tasks dispatched by string name
Plugins loaded through entry points declared in pyproject.toml
